target.title: fix(media): bound hung remote downloads in media store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users and gateway paths that persist remote media through `saveMediaSource()` would hang indefinitely when a media URL accepted the TCP connection but never sent response headers, or sent a partial body and then stalled. Only a max-bytes cap existed; there was no header or idle-read timeout, so requests, temp files, and caller chains could stay pinned forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add 30s response-header and idle-body timeouts to `downloadToFile()` in the media store path, matching the hang-bounding intent already used by `src/media/fetch.ts` / web-media reads. On timeout, destroy the request/response, clear timers, delete the temp file, and reject with an explicit stall/timeout error. Timeouts are overridable in tests via `setMediaStoreNetworkDepsForTest`.

This does not change MIME sniffing, redirect header stripping, or the 5MB size cap.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung or adversarial media URL could block `saveMediaSource()` (including gateway managed-image ingestion) with no recovery besides process restart.

**After:** Stalled header waits and idle body reads fail within 30s, temp files are removed, and callers get a clear timeout/stall error.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/media/store.ts` (`downloadToFile`)
- Caller under test: production `saveMediaSource(httpUrl)` against a real local `node:http` server
- Regression: `src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts`
- Sibling redirect suite still green: `src/media/store.redirect.test.ts`

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > times out when the server accepts a connection but never sends headers 78ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > times out when the response body stalls after partial data 52ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > still saves when the remote body completes before idle timeout 4855ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 73.15s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `saveMediaSource()` remote downloads no longer hang forever on servers that accept connections without sending headers, or that stall after partial body data; temp files are cleaned up after timeout.
- **Canonical reachability path:** gateway/managed-image and other callers → `saveMediaSource(url)` → `downloadToFile()` → header timer / idle body timer → reject + temp cleanup.
- **Boundary crossed:** Untrusted remote HTTP(S) media source → local media-store temp file / saved media ID.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Aligns store downloads with the existing media `fetch.ts` / web-media header + idle-read hang bounds; keeps SSRF pinned-hostname lookup and redirect header stripping unchanged.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Node source checkout with a real `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` (pinned lookup override for loopback) exercising production `saveMediaSource`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ ... > times out when the server accepts a connection but never sends headers 78ms
 ✓ ... > times out when the response body stalls after partial data 52ms
 ✓ ... > still saves when the remote body completes before idle timeout
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 73.15s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Hang-headers rejects with `timed out waiting for response headers after 40ms` (test override); stall-body rejects with `stalled: no data received for 40ms`; both leave zero files under the media root. Successful short responses still save.
- **What was not tested:** Live public HTTPS media URLs; gateway managed-image end-to-end UI path; redirect-during-timeout races.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Long session histories make the Control UI sidebar difficult to scan because every session is rendered at once. ## Why This Change Was Made This PR makes the sidebar start with 10 sessions and reveal 10 more per action.
